run.model: glm-5.3 (LLM API labeling via Claude Code CLI, temperature 0)
run.prompt_contract: Per-batch LLM payload: pass descriptor (pass_id/cwes/focus), the candidate CSV rows (node/callable/flowKind/receiver/moduleHint/argIndex/file/line), selected source snippets (the LLM read openapi_python_client/__init__.py, cli.py, config.py, utils.py, parser/openapi.py, parser/reference.py in full), and framework hints from references/python.md + references/patterns.md (typer CLI detected; no web framework, so HTTP-shaped families are N/A). Rubric: source = genuine untrusted input boundary; sink = actual file read/write/delete/unpack/file-response; sanitizer = proven containment neutralization; summary = helper flow step; none = unrelated. Conservative recall, JSON-only output, temperature 0.
run.batch_policy: 7 batches, stable sizes (11/12/7/15/19/17/7); all 88 candidate rows labeled in one pass each; no re-ask was needed because no final label fell below the 0.55 confidence threshold except entries intentionally recorded as candidate/unknown for human review (config-content sources at 0.50-0.55 and subprocess-cwd sinks at 0.55).

label.rationale: Return value of httpx.get(url) in _get_document carries the remote OpenAPI document body (consumed as response.content, then yaml.safe_load). Fetching externally-authored specs over --url is the tool's core use case, so the response body is attacker-influenced document content. The URL itself is an operator-selected endpoint (Pass 3 material); the returned body is the Pass 1 input boundary.

Attribute read of the remote response body: the fetched document bytes enter local flow as yaml_bytes and are parsed at :80. Direct untrusted content boundary; fully attacker-controlled when --url points at a server the operator does not control.

Return value of path.read_bytes() is the --path OpenAPI document CONTENT. The file is operator-selected (the CLI user passes --path), but the document itself is typically authored by a third party (a downloaded spec), so its content is untrusted of the same shape as the URL case and flows straight into yaml.safe_load. The path VALUE is operator-trust and is not treated as attacker-controlled (see the sink labeling of :76).

Primary document parse boundary: every remote document field (info.title, components.schemas names+titles, paths -> operations -> tags) enters local flow as the returned dict and later determines generated filesystem names. safe_load is safe for deserialization (Pass 6), but the parsed VALUES are untrusted for Pass 1 path construction.

Class-attribute read feeding project_name (line 94 'self.project_name_override or <title f-string>'), which becomes Path.cwd() / project_name at :95. The value originates from the --config YAML (config.py:29 sets Project.project_name_override). The config file is operator-selected (same trust domain as the CLI user), but a shared/committed config consumed in CI can be externally authored: retained as source with candidate classification for human review; downgrade to fp if the config file is deemed fully trusted. MANUAL REVIEW POINT.

Remote info.title (copied into GeneratorData.title at openapi.py:311) is read inside the project_name f-string. Only cosmetic shaping follows (replace(' ', '-'), lower(), '-client' suffix) - no '/', backslash or '..' handling - so a title containing '../' or a leading '/' fully controls project_dir = Path.cwd() / project_name and every mkdir/write_text/rmtree below it. Strongest Pass 1 source.

Same operator-trust config caveat as project_name_override; candidate pending review. MANUAL REVIEW POINT.
